clue.text: Being green will involve experiencing some dampness there

definitions.text: Being green will involve experiencing some dampness there

parts.note: surface reading: a novice or naive person, or perhaps someone feeling sick
setter's reading: the idiom says an inexperienced person is still wet in a particular spot on the head

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about where someone who is green will feel damp.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'wet behind the ears' means naive or inexperienced, like a newborn not yet dried off; the clue asks for the place where the wetness sits.
explanation.definitionFit: Being green means being naive, and the idiom locates that innocence as moisture in a spot on the head.

clue.text: Duck low to get cover

parts.note: the eider is a sea duck
feeling low is feeling down

explanation.surface: Advice to crouch low in order to take cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' and 'low' read as instructions to crouch, but they are a bird and a mood.
explanation.definitionFit: An eiderdown is a quilt, a cover for a bed, originally filled with the soft feathers of that bird.

clue.text: Enthusiastic over wife coming along with you

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first part sits above the next one in the column

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A keen spouse tagging along with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in tow follows closely behind you, as an accompanying companion or a towed vehicle does.

clue.text: Setter perhaps has seven they say for each of yours

definitions.text: Setter perhaps has seven they say for each of yours

parts.note: surface reading: the crossword compiler talking about themselves

parts.words: has seven they say for each of yours
parts.note: setter's reading: a setter is a breed of dog, and popular lore says such an animal ages seven units for every one a human does

explanation.surface: The crossword setter apparently claims seven of something for every one of the solver's.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter is a gun dog; folk wisdom holds that one human year equals seven in a dog's life.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the unit of canine ageing, reckoned as seven to one human twelvemonth.

clue.text: Barely able to put together complex set

indicators.note: putting things together means joining them side by side, so the two parts are placed one after the other

parts.note: a complex task is a difficult one
to set something down is to place it

explanation.surface: Someone struggling to assemble a complicated kit.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is normally followed by 'to', as in 'hard put to explain', which is why the definition reads 'Barely able' with 'to' joining it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hard put to do something is an idiom for managing it only with great difficulty.

clue.text: Should Ken sabotage these hunters?

indicators.note: to sabotage something is to wreck it, so the letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: the letters as printed

explanation.surface: A question of whether a hunt saboteur named Ken should disrupt these hunters.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests anti-hunting protest, which fits the answer, a breed of hunting dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Elkhounds are Scandinavian dogs bred to track and hold large game such as moose.

clue.text: Introducing really healthy organic meals benefits figure

indicators.note: what introduces each word is its opening letter, so only the leading letters are kept

parts.note: the initial letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A diet blurb: wholesome organic food is good for your figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure' reads as body shape, but it means a geometric shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhomb, or rhombus, is a geometric shape: a parallelogram with four equal sides.

clue.text: It's used for shooting horse with record speed

parts.note: a colt is a young male horse
single records spin at 45 revolutions per minute

explanation.surface: Grim talk of a gun for putting down a horse, or a fast-galloping one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record speed' suggests a fastest time, but it is the playing speed of a vinyl single.
explanation.definitionFit: The Colt .45 is a famous revolver, a weapon made for firing bullets.

clue.text: Opposition to unreliable poor getting a decent hand

parts.note: the opposite of unreliable or crooked is honest, straight
the opposite of poor is well off, flush; 'Opposition to' applies here as well

explanation.surface: Political commentary: resisting the untrustworthy poor wins a fair deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opposition to' governs both words, asking for antonyms of 'unreliable' and 'poor'.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker a straight flush, five suited cards in sequence, is one of the strongest holdings you can be dealt.

clue.text: Lord gets a treatment from experienced performer

indicators.note: a treatment is a reworking or handling, so these letters are processed into a new order

parts.note: the letters as printed

explanation.surface: A peer receives medical care from a seasoned actor.
explanation.definitionFit: An old stager is a veteran, someone long practised at something, originally an actor long on the boards.

clue.text: Whip is extremely keen — when available

indicators.note: extremely points at the extremes of the word, its first and final letters

parts.note: the two end letters of keen
a product that is out has been released and can be got

explanation.surface: A whip is very eager whenever it is to hand.
explanation.walkthrough: A knout is an old Russian flogging whip; the word is rare, so the wordplay does the work.
explanation.definitionFit: The knout was a heavy many-thonged lash used for punishment in imperial Russia.

clue.text: Host project launch

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to hold a party, as in giving one
second meaning: to cast or hurl forward
third meaning: to send something flying, like a ball

explanation.surface: Three words that sound like a plan to start a venture.
explanation.walkthrough: Three separate meanings here, not two: one verb covers holding a party, casting forward and hurling.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers staging a party ('throw a do') as well as propelling something through the air.

clue.text: Plant which could discharge boron to cause intoxication

indicators.note: the plant could let go of the chemical element, so that element is sitting inside the plant's name

parts.note: a giddy high
B is the chemical symbol for boron

explanation.surface: A plant that releases boron to make people drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: take B out of the plant and you get the intoxication, so B sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphorbia is the spurge genus, a large group of plants with milky sap that includes the poinsettia.

clue.text: Casual type of relationship old queen has available

parts.note: an on-off relationship keeps stopping and starting
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

explanation.surface: An aged queen is open to a casual fling.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods on offer are for sale or being made available to take.

clue.text: Anticipation of battle to acquire minerals

indicators.note: acquiring something means taking it in, so one word swallows the other

parts.note: a battle is a fight
ores are mined mineral deposits

explanation.surface: Expecting a war over mineral resources.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a conflict over mining rights; 'of' simply joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Foresight is the ability to look ahead and prepare for what is coming.

clue.text: Kick around family that's failing

indicators.note: around says the first word wraps itself about the second

parts.note: a sharp flavour, a kick
one's kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: Booting a ball about among relatives who aren't doing well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kick' reads as a verb, but it is the noun meaning a sharp taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanking is informal for performing very badly or collapsing, as a share price or a film can.

clue.text: I trade in perfect place …

parts.note: taken as written
to trade is to deal
someone in is at home

explanation.surface: An estate agent's boast about swapping into a dream house, continued in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to 19-down so the two read as one sentence; it carries no wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal home is a dream dwelling, the best place one could live; the phrase names a long-running British home exhibition.

clue.text: Shoot short camp routine

indicators.note: something short is cut down, so each of the following words loses its final letter

parts.note: a tent is camping shelter
a drill is a set routine or exercise

explanation.surface: Filming a brief scene of a holiday-camp exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' applies to both words, docking the last letter of each.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendril is a slender climbing shoot of a plant such as a vine or pea.

clue.text: … that's occupied, and looking well used

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a house people have inhabited
second meaning: comfortably worn, showing signs of daily use

explanation.surface: Continuing 17-down: a dream house that is inhabited and shows its wear.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading ellipsis joins this to the clue before; the two meanings are the participle and the adjective form of one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A dwelling inhabited is one people resided in; as an adjective the phrase describes a room that looks homely and worn.

clue.text: Disagreement voiced on the way down

indicators.note: voiced means spoken, so what counts is how the phrase sounds rather than its spelling

parts.note: a way down a slope is a descent

explanation.surface: An argument shouted on the descent of a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissent is the open expression of disagreement with an official or majority view.

clue.text: Engineers break word, abandoning alternative for dodgy sites

indicators.note: to engineer is to contrive or construct, so the remaining letters are built into a new order
abandoning means leaving something behind, so a word for an option is dropped from the letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Engineers go back on a promise, leaving the options for shady websites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineers' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is a verb telling you to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The dark web is the hidden part of the internet, reached through special software and known for illicit trading.

clue.text: Tackle defender — it will avoid embarrassment

parts.note: to tackle a problem is to face it
one who saves, as a goalkeeper defends

explanation.surface: A footballer urging a tackle on a defender, then an aside about avoiding shame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tackle' and 'defender' set up a football picture, but tackle means to confront.
explanation.definitionFit: A face-saver is an action or excuse that lets someone keep their dignity and avoid humiliation.

clue.text: Country church sits on return of priest

indicators.note: in a down clue, sitting on something means being above it, so this part comes first

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the word for the cleric runs backwards

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: A rural church built over a returning clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' looks like an adjective for the church; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Chile is a nation running along the Pacific coast of South America.

clue.text: Only some of Mughal alphabet is permitted in Islam

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is taken, so the solution lies inside the words that follow

parts.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A claim that only part of an Indian dynasty's script is religiously acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mughals were the Muslim emperors of India, fitting the Islamic surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Halal is the Arabic term for what Islamic law allows, especially food prepared in accordance with it.

clue.text: Funny reaction about origin of tantric yoga format

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the laugh is placed around the single letter

parts.note: the sound of laughter

indicators.note: the origin of a word is where it begins, its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of tantric

explanation.surface: Someone laughs at a style of tantric yoga.
explanation.definitionFit: Hatha is the branch of yoga built on physical postures and breathing, the kind most Western classes teach.

clue.text: Very good case for one in Scotland being competitive

indicators.note: a case holds something inside it, so the first abbreviation encloses the second word

parts.note: VG is the standard abbreviation for very good
yin is the Scots form of one

explanation.surface: A fine example of a court case in Scotland about competition.
explanation.walkthrough: Scots dialect uses yin for one, as in 'the big yin'.
explanation.definitionFit: Vying means contending or competing with rivals for something.

clue.text: Strike spoils travelling around in hills

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: downs are rolling chalk hills in southern England

indicators.note: travelling around means turning back on itself, so the word for plunder runs backwards

parts.note: loot is plunder, the spoils of war

explanation.surface: Plunder carried across hilly country is struck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' could be a verb to hit; here it is industrial action.
explanation.definitionFit: To down tools is to stop work, typically in protest, which is what a strike is.

clue.text: Bizarre BBC rant sealed extra coverage

indicators.note: something bizarre is strange and out of order, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: the letters as printed

explanation.surface: A strange tirade from the broadcaster sealed its expanded news coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coverage' suggests broadcasting, but the definition means double protection.
explanation.definitionFit: Belt and braces is a British idiom for taking two precautions where one would do, like holding up trousers both ways.
